answer: Dawn-faucet bond: one onyx root mints a single nontransferable nectar each dawn for judged work, however many keys hang from it. The kth live key under that root must lock k^2 nectar; the first pays one, while n added heads need sum k^2 ≈ n^3/3 nectar, which takes that many dawn from one root—unparallelizable, unsplittable; more roots mean buying unrelated onyx.
